title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 63 (Issue of bonus shares)

content.overview: A company may issue fully paid-up bonus shares out of free reserves, the securities premium account or the capital redemption reserve, subject to section 63's conditions; reserves created by revaluation of assets cannot be capitalised, and bonus shares cannot be issued in lieu of dividend.
content.glance: A company may issue fully paid-up bonus shares out of free reserves, the securities premium account or the capital redemption reserve, subject to section 63's conditions; reserves created by revaluation of assets cannot be capitalised, and bonus shares cannot be issued in lieu of dividend.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 63 (Issue of bonus shares). A company may issue fully paid-up bonus shares to its members out of free reserves, the securities premium account or the capital redemption reserve account; reserves created by revaluation of assets cannot be capitalised for this purpose. Before capitalising profits or reserves, the company must satisfy the statutory conditions: authority in its articles; authorisation at a general meeting on the Board's recommendation; no default in payment of interest or principal in respect of fixed deposits or debt securities; no default in employee statutory dues such as provident-fund contributions, gratuity and bonus; any partly paid-up shares outstanding on the allotment date must be made fully paid; and prescribed conditions must be met. Bonus shares must not be issued in lieu of dividend. Verify applicable rules and any other transaction-specific restrictions before treating an issue as ready.

sections.heading: Permitted sources
sections.body: Bonus shares may be issued out of free reserves, the securities premium account or the capital redemption reserve account. Reserves created by revaluation of assets must not be capitalised for this purpose.

sections.heading: Corporate authority
sections.body: The articles must authorise the issue, and the company must authorise it in general meeting on the Board's recommendation.

sections.heading: Debt and employee statutory dues
sections.body: The company must not have defaulted in payment of interest or principal on fixed deposits or debt securities, or in payment of employee statutory dues such as provident-fund contributions, gratuity and bonus.

sections.heading: Fully paid shares and prescribed conditions
sections.body: Any partly paid-up shares outstanding on the date of allotment must be made fully paid-up, and the company must comply with prescribed conditions.

sections.heading: No bonus in lieu of dividend
sections.body: Bonus shares must not be issued in lieu of dividend.

examples.title: In lieu of dividend
examples.body: A resolution declaring bonus shares instead of a cash dividend already recommended is outside s. 63.

examples.title: Revaluation reserve
examples.body: A revaluation surplus is not a permitted source for bonus shares.

hypotheticals.question: A company wants to issue bonus shares by capitalising a reserve created through revaluation of assets. Is that permitted?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 63 excludes reserves created by revaluation of assets from the permitted sources for a bonus issue.

hypotheticals.question: A company has partly paid shares outstanding on the proposed allotment date. What must it do?
hypotheticals.analysis: The partly paid-up shares outstanding on the date of allotment must be made fully paid-up, in addition to satisfying the other section 63 conditions.

distinctions.title: Bonus issue and dividend
distinctions.left: A bonus issue capitalises permitted reserves into fully paid-up shares.
distinctions.right: A dividend is a distribution under the applicable dividend provisions; bonus shares cannot be issued in lieu of dividend.

rows.right: Distributable profits and applicable dividend rules

misconceptions.trap: Treating any reserve, including a revaluation reserve, as available for bonus shares.
misconceptions.correction: Section 63 permits only free reserves, securities premium and capital redemption reserve; revaluation reserves are excluded.

misconceptions.trap: Treating Board recommendation alone as sufficient approval.
misconceptions.correction: The articles must authorise the issue and a general meeting must authorise it on the Board's recommendation.

misconceptions.trap: Issuing bonus shares while statutory conditions are unmet or in lieu of dividend.
misconceptions.correction: Check debt/employee-dues defaults, fully paid status and prescribed conditions; bonus shares cannot be issued in lieu of dividend.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Which reserves may fund a bonus issue under section 63?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Free reserves, the securities premium account and the capital redemption reserve account; reserves created by revaluation of assets are excluded.

questionsAndAnswers.question: May bonus shares be issued in lieu of dividend?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. Section 63(3) prohibits bonus shares in lieu of dividend.
